# @ratmath/stats

> Probability and statistics for RatMath: exact finite probability, certified distributions, seeded data generation with noise, tests, regression, rank tests, the bootstrap, Markov chains and Bayesian updating. Part of the RatMath Shelf; numbers come from @ratmath/core (a peer dependency). ESM: `import * as stats from "@ratmath/stats"`.

Built from 0.3.0, commit 8473337 plus uncommitted changes. `file:line` is relative to the package root (also node_modules/@ratmath/stats/); on GitHub: https://github.com/ratmath/stats/blob/8473337/<file>#L<line>. Docs pages are under https://ratmath.com/stats/. Full types: index.d.ts.

Types: `type Num = Rational | number | bigint | string`; `type Value = Rational | RationalInterval`; `type Datum = Num | RationalInterval | [Num, Num]`; `type Seed = number | string | bigint`; `type Alternative = "two-sided" | "greater" | "less"`; `type Event<T> = ((outcome: T) => boolean) | Set<T> | T`; `type QuantileMethod = "linear" | "weibull" | "hazen" | "median-unbiased" | "inverse" | "lower" | "higher" | "nearest" | "midpoint" | "halves" | "tukey"`; `type DensityPiece = [string, [Num | "inf" | "-inf", Num | "inf" | "-inf"]]`; `type Family = "normal" | "exponential" | "poisson" | "bernoulli" | "binomial" | "geometric" | "uniform" | "gamma" | "beta" | "lognormal"`; `type Predictors = Num[] | Num[][] | Record<string, Num[]>`; `type Source = Continuous | Discrete | Finite<any> | ((rng: Random) => Num) | Num`; `type DataSource<D> = { model: Model; n: number } | { draw: (rng: Random, run: number) => D }`; `type RankMethod = "auto" | "exact" | "normal"`; `type State = string | number`

## Docs

- https://ratmath.com/stats/llms-full.txt: every page below as Markdown, each with a runnable example
- Pages: index (Overview), reference (Reference), explore (Explore), finite-probability (Finite probability), discrete-distributions (Discrete distributions), descriptive (Descriptive statistics), exact-tests (Exact tests), continuous-distributions (Continuous distributions), densities (Your own densities), certified-answers (Certified answers), sampling (Seeded sampling), models (Models with noise), experiments (Experiments), means (Tests for means), variances-proportions (Variances and proportions), chi-square (Chi-square tests), power (Power and sample size), estimation (Fitting distributions), testing-the-tests (Testing the tests), regression (Linear regression), anova (Analysis of variance), rank-tests (Rank tests), kolmogorov-smirnov (Kolmogorov–Smirnov), bootstrap (The bootstrap), markov-chains (Markov chains), bayesian-updating (Bayesian updating)

## Example

```js
import { show, binomial, normal, howOften } from "@ratmath/stats";
// One question, three kinds of answer.
// How likely are 11 or more heads in 16 tosses of a fair coin?
const X = binomial(16, "1/2");
console.log("exact:     ", String(X.sf(10)), "=", show(X.sf(10), 6));

// The same from the normal curve with a continuity correction: certified, and an approximation.
const approx = normal(8, 2).sf("10.5");      // mean 8, standard deviation 2
console.log("certified: ", show(approx, 12), "(the normal curve's answer, to 12 places)");

// And by tossing coins: simulated, with its own error bars.
const sim = howOften({ draw: (rng) => X.sample(rng), event: (k) => k >= 11, runs: 4000, seed: 1 });
console.log("simulated: ", String(sim));
sim.compare(X.sf(10))   // is the exact answer inside the simulation's interval?
```
